Af. - אָקֵים, אוֹקִים, , אוֹקֵי
1) to put up, erect; to appoint, place; to maintain. Targum Onkelos Shemot XL, 2 תָּקִים (ed. Berliner (editor of Targum Onkelos) and Yerushalmi תְּקִים). Ib. 18 ואָקֵים (ed. Berliner (editor of Targum Onkelos) ואָקֵים and ואֵקִים). Targum Onkelos Devarim XXV, 7 לאָקָמָא ed. Berliner (editor of Targum Onkelos) (oth. ed. לַאֲקָ׳; Yerushalmi למִיקְמָא). Targum Psalms LXXVIII, 13. Targum Mishlei XXIX, 4; and from—Bava Metzia 39ᵇ מוֹקְמִינָן … לינוקא we (the court) appoint a guardian over it in behalf of the minor. Ib. מיגו דמוֹקִים … מוקמינן וכ׳ since one appoints a guardian for the one-sixth portion, we may just as well appoint one for the other sixth. Bava Batra 33ᵃ אוֹקְמָהּ … בידיה R. Ḥ. placed it in his possession, i.e. decided that it belonged to him. Ib. 34ᵃ מוֹקְמִינָן לה בידיה we would place (or leave) it in his possession; and see from—Taanit 8ᵃ, and from אוקים … אמורא, see אֲמוֹרָא.—Esp. a) to put a case, to treat with reference to. Bava Batra 44ᵃ ולוֹקְמָהּ בגזלן why does he not put the case as treating of a robber?; ולוקמה ביורש let him say, it refers to the case of an heir!; and from—b) to let stand, place, leave (under the presumption). Ketubot 12ᵇ, and e. אוקי ממונא בחזקת מריה leave the money where it is, on the presumption that it belongs to its present owner, i.e. possession has the benefit of the doubt. Ib. אוֹקְמָהּ אחזקה leave the woman in her ascertained condition (see חֲזָקָה), i.e. consider her as having married as a virgin. Yevamot 31ᵃ אוקי תרי להדי תרי ואשה אוקמה אחזקה leave the two witnesses (on the one side) against the two witnesses (on the other side), and leave the woman &c.; and from—c) to establish, prove. Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 6, end ורבנן מוֹקְמִין מהאי קרא וכ׳ and the Rabbis prove from this verse, that as atonement takes place in day-time, so &c.; and e.—d) א׳ טבאות [to place right] to guarantee, secure. Yerushalmi Gittin I, end, 43ᵈ אנן בעי תְּקִימִינָן ט׳ (not טבאת) we want thee to secure us (against an eventual loss of the money which thou art collecting from us for our creditors); בההוא דלא יכיל למִיקְמָה גרמיה ט׳ in the case of one who has no opportunity to secure himself (who cannot get a collector to take the risk), ברם ההוא דיכיל למיקמה וכ׳ but if he finds a collector to take the risk, he may take it away from the one and give it to the other; Yerushalmi Kiddushin III, 64ᵃ.—
2) (see עָמַד) to make consistent, curdle. Pirkei Avot Zar. 35ᵃ [read:] כיון דאוֹקְמֵיה איסורא הוא דקא מוֹקִים ליה וכ׳ (see Manuscript Munich in Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l., and note) since it had the effect of curdling the milk, it is the forbidden matter that gave it substance, and therefore it (that forbidden substance) is to be considered as if it were there in its natural state. 1) as preceding Piël, to establish, confirm, fulfill &c. Targum Onkelos Devarim XXXII, 8 (Yerushalmi Af.). Targum Bamidbar XXX, 14. Targum Isaiah l. common gender. Targum Psalms CXIX, 106; and from—Nedarim 70ᵃ דהא קַיְּימֵיה לנדריה היום (not קיימי, see Rashi) for he has confirmed the vow to-day. Ib. (h. form) כיון דקִיְּימוֹ קִיְּימוֹ since he once confirmed it, it remains confirmed. Ketubot 19ᵃ זילו קַיְּימוּ שטרייכו go and get evidence for the identification of your documents, and then come to court. comments.en: This is referring to the presumptive status of the bride’s body; since she was born as a virgin, she maintains that status until proven otherwise. The Rid and the Rosh add that although the bride does not receive payment of her marriage contract before she enters the wedding canopy, fundamentally, she is entitled to it even after betrothal. They did not want to rely solely on her presumptive status of virginity; that presumption itself was undermined, as she is no longer a virgin when the claim is made. Later commentaries discuss this subject extensively, from various perspectives (see Maharam Schiff and Shev Shemateta).
comments.he: חזקה זו היא חזקת הגוף של האשה, שכיון שנולדה בתולה יש לומר שנשארה בתולה עד שעה שנודע שאינה כן. והרי"ד והרא"ש כותבים שיש להוסיף לכך גם טעם אחר — שיש כתובה לארוסה, רק שאין הכתובה מגיעה לה אלא לאחר כניסתה לחופה. כי על חזקת הגוף בלבד אין להסתמך שהרי היא מעורערת כאן שהרי היא בעולה לפנינו. ואחרונים מאריכים לדון בנושא זה מכמה צדדים (וראה במהר"ם שיף ובשב שמעתתא שעוסקים בכך).

sections.en: Alternatively, Rav Naḥman could have said to you: Rabban Gamliel says his ruling only there, where we say: Establish her legal status according to her presumptive status as a virgin, and the husband’s claim seeks to undermine that presumptive status. However here, what presumptive status does this claimant have supporting the claim that another owes him money? Therefore, even Rabban Gamliel would concede that his certain claim does not prevail.
